3 John 1.summary: The elder writes unto the wellbeloved Gaius, whom he loves in the truth, wishing above all things that he may prosper and be in health, even as his soul prospereth (3 John 1:1–2). He rejoiced greatly when the brethren came and testified of the truth that is in Gaius, even as he walketh in the truth, for he hath no greater joy than to hear that his children walk in truth (3 John 1:3–4). Gaius doeth faithfully whatsoever he doeth to the brethren and to strangers, who have borne witness of his charity before the church, and he will do well to bring them forward on their journey after a godly sort, because for his name's sake they went forth, taking nothing of the Gentiles, so we ought to receive such, that we might be fellowhelpers to the truth (3 John 1:5–8). The elder wrote unto the church, but Diotrephes, who loveth to have the preeminence among them, receiveth us not, and if the elder comes, he will remember his deeds, prating against us with malicious words, and neither doth he himself receive the brethren, and forbiddeth them that would, and casteth them out of the church (3 John 1:9–10). Gaius is told to follow not that which is evil but that which is good, for he that doeth good is of God, but he that doeth evil hath not seen God, and Demetrius hath good report of all men and of the truth itself (3 John 1:11–12). The elder had many things to write but will not with ink and pen, trusting shortly to see Gaius and speak face to face, and he closes with peace and greetings from the friends (3 John 1:13–14).
3 John 1.whereWeAre: 3 John follows 2 John and is the elder's letter to the wellbeloved Gaius. It praises him for walking in truth and for kindness to the brethren and strangers, tells of Diotrephes who loveth the preeminence, and commends Demetrius (1:1-14). Jude follows.

keyFigures.name: The elder
keyFigures.role: Writes to Gaius, rejoices that his children walk in truth, and will remember the deeds of Diotrephes (1:1,4,10).

keyFigures.name: Gaius
keyFigures.role: The wellbeloved, who walks in the truth and doeth faithfully to the brethren and to strangers (1:1,3,5).

keyFigures.name: The brethren and strangers
keyFigures.role: They testified of Gaius' truth and went forth for his name's sake, taking nothing of the Gentiles (1:3,5-7).

keyFigures.name: Diotrephes
keyFigures.role: Loveth to have the preeminence, receiveth not the elder, prates with malicious words, and casteth them out of the church (1:9-10).

keyFigures.name: Demetrius
keyFigures.role: Hath good report of all men and of the truth itself (1:12).

keyFigures.name: The church
keyFigures.role: Before which Gaius's charity was witnessed, and from which Diotrephes casts out those who would receive the brethren (1:6,9-10).

keyThemes.explanation: The elder has no greater joy than to hear that his children walk in truth, and Gaius walketh in the truth (1:3-4).

keyThemes.theme: Hospitality as partnership in gospel work
